readout_other: Hippocampal/cerebellar single-unit and LFP (ERSP, phase-amplitude coupling); ECoG in 4-AP seizure model; cFos immunofluorescence (slice and cleared whole brain)
direction_notes: Cerebellar tFUS at PRF 1 kHz and 10 kHz excited cerebellum; 10 kHz favoured inhibition of hippocampal neurons; at 10 kHz tFUS reduced ECoG power in a 4-AP seizure model.
safety_notes: H&E staining showed no tissue damage after stimulation with these parameters.

exposures.label: Cerebellum-targeted tFUS, PRF 1 kHz vs 10 kHz (plus 10 kHz in 4-AP seizure model)

device.model: V301-SU flat transducer with 2 mm collimator

timing.protocol_description: FF 500 kHz, DC 50 %, PRF 1 or 10 kHz with burst duration adjusted to keep DC constant (burst duration not given in text); UD 500 ms, ISI 10 s; 20 min for cFos. Seizure model: PRF 10 kHz, DC 50 %, UD 1 s, ISI 5 s, 10 min.

source_quotes.n_subjects: We further recorded 62 hippocampal neurons from 13 rats subject to PRF of 1 kHz (LFUS) and 10 kHz (HFUS), respectively, in cerebellumtargeted tFUS (Fig. 3A).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: In this study, the FF was kept at 500 kHz, which is within the optimal range for stimulating intact brain [7].

flags.reason: Converted from 0.21 MPa; measured by hydrophone without cranium. The paper does not say which PRF these values correspond to.
Converted from 0.10 MPa; hydrophone measurement through a freshly excised rat cranium in water (not brain tissue).
500 ms in main experiments and 1 s in the seizure model; the 1 s value is quoted in methods 2.14 and 3.x, not under this quote.
Burst duration per pulse stated only in a figure and not in text.
13 rats in the PRF recording experiment; other experiments used 3 per group (GsMTx4), 5 per group (cFos slices, seizure), 1 per group (whole-brain cFos); overlap not stated.
Control rats received no tFUS; a separate artefact check aimed ultrasound at the upper part of the electrode array.
Epilepsy refers to an acute 4-AP seizure model; the rest of the work is in non-epileptic rats.
